how_these_run: By hand. No runner reads this file: run-all.mjs discovers only *.test.mjs, and `claude plugin eval` is early access and absent from this build. The method — give an agent the prompt verbatim, then count Skill calls in its transcript rather than believing its self-report — is in evals/README.md under 'The trigger cases'.

evals.prompt: Ask codex to review this diff.
evals.expected_output: Fires. The user named Codex explicitly; run at --level read against the repo.
expectations: Invokes the codex-delegate skill
Chooses --level read, because a review needs no write access
Does NOT use the openai-codex plugin (codex:rescue / codex-companion.mjs)
evals.covers: trigger: user names Codex

evals.prompt: Run this past the other model and see if it disagrees with me.
evals.expected_output: Fires. 'The other model' names a second opinion without saying Codex.
expectations: Invokes the codex-delegate skill
Chooses --level read
evals.covers: trigger: indirect reference to a second model

evals.prompt: Set up a panel of four reviewers to tear this design apart before I commit to it.
evals.expected_output: Fires. A panel of only Claudes shares one bias; the dissenting seat should be Codex.
expectations: Considers giving at least one seat to Codex via codex-delegate
Does NOT hand the whole panel to Codex
Keeps the remaining seats as Claude subagents
evals.covers: trigger: panel needing a decorrelated seat

evals.expected_output: Fires. Two failed hypotheses, and the premise is true by construction — the bug is in the prompt.
expectations: Invokes the codex-delegate skill
Hands the seat both refuted hypotheses, so the turn does not spend itself re-testing them
Chooses --level read: the function is in the prompt, and no repository, test suite or dependency was named
evals.covers: trigger: dead end after two failed hypotheses (self-contained, no repo state)

evals.expected_output: Fires. A second implementation for comparison, with the subject supplied so the premise holds.
expectations: Invokes the codex-delegate skill
Uses an isolated worktree rather than the main working tree
evals.covers: trigger: second implementation for comparison (self-contained)

evals.prompt: What is the capital of France?
evals.expected_output: Does NOT fire. Trivia.
expectations: Does NOT invoke the codex-delegate skill
Answers directly
evals.covers: negative: trivia

evals.prompt: Find every file that imports TokenModel.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT fire for a Codex seat. Mechanical fact-gathering is where the default composition is ZERO: decorrelation buys nothing when there is nothing to disagree about, and each seat costs real memory and a turn-overhead floor (the measured figures are in parity.md, 'Fan-out and reporting').
expectations: Does NOT invoke the codex-delegate skill
Uses local search tools instead
Does NOT read 'fan out' as a reason to add a Codex seat
evals.covers: negative: mechanical fan-out — the default composition here is zero Codex, not one

evals.expected_output: Does NOT fire. A one-identifier rename in code supplied in the prompt is faster done directly than delegated.
expectations: Does NOT invoke the codex-delegate skill
Performs the rename directly, on the code given
evals.covers: negative: trivial edit (self-contained — the earlier version named an identifier that does not exist in this repo, so the expectation was unachievable and the case measured nothing)

evals.prompt: Open packages/core/src/codex-samples.ts and fix the type error on line 12.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT fire. 'codex' appears only as part of a filename, not as a request for the tool.
expectations: Does NOT invoke the codex-delegate skill
Treats 'codex' as part of a path, not as a tool name
evals.covers: negative: the word codex as a substring, adversarial

evals.prompt: Have codex run the full test suite in an isolated copy and tell me what fails.
evals.expected_output: Fires, and must pick the worktree path and dispose of the tree itself.
expectations: Invokes the codex-delegate skill
Creates a git worktree and passes --level write with --network, because a fresh tree installs its own dependencies
Removes the worktree itself after harvesting, and does not ask Codex to remove it
evals.covers: behaviour: worktree lifecycle

evals.prompt: Codex reviewed the file and says all the tests pass. Should I merge?
evals.expected_output: Must not take the claim at face value: prose is not a receipt, and the report says which commands ran.
expectations: Does NOT accept 'the tests pass' from Codex's prose
Checks the command list or the JSON report for a command with a numeric exitCode
Names what is still unproven rather than endorsing the merge on the seat's word
evals.covers: behaviour: the honesty gate proves a command ran, not the right one

evals.prompt: Delegate this to codex on GPT-5.6-sol at maximum reasoning.
evals.expected_output: Fires, passes the named model, and does not silently accept an unsupported effort.
expectations: Invokes the codex-delegate skill with --model gpt-5.6-sol
Passes --effort max through: the driver validates against the advertised ladder (up to max/ultra), and a value the server refuses comes back as exit 2 carrying the server's own list
Does NOT hardcode a model when the user has not named one
evals.covers: behaviour: model and effort are per call, never hardcoded

evals.expected_output: Fires. Must say up front that the seat cannot commit and that the branch is the caller's step.
expectations: Recognises that a Codex seat cannot commit: its sandbox ends at the tree it was given, and committing needs the repository's git directory
Says so before running, rather than reporting a failed commit afterwards
Proposes handing back the work as a diff (worktreeDiffPath, or the live tree) and committing it on the branch itself
evals.covers: behaviour: a seat writes, the caller commits (self-contained)

evals.prompt: Fan out ten codex agents to audit each package in parallel.
evals.expected_output: Fires, but must cap the fan-out on memory grounds rather than obeying the number.
expectations: Invokes the codex-delegate skill
Warns that concurrency is memory-bound, from the per-seat figures parity.md records under 'Fan-out and reporting' rather than a number of its own
Proposes running in waves instead of ten at once, or checks free memory first
evals.covers: behaviour: concurrency budget is per machine

evals.prompt: Codex said the lock is safe because `wx` is exclusive. I disagree: exclusive creation says nothing about the RECLAIM path, where a peer can unlink a lock it did not create. Put that back to codex and see if it holds up.
evals.expected_output: Fires and continues the EXISTING thread. The counter-argument is supplied, so the only question is whether the agent resumes rather than restating context in a fresh thread.
expectations: Uses --resume <threadId> if a thread id from the prior round is available
Does NOT restate the whole original context in a fresh thread
Knows a recall-only follow-up needs --allow-no-commands
evals.covers: behaviour: multi-round via thread resume (self-contained — the earlier version left the disputed claim and the counter-argument blank, so the agent had nothing to send and refusing to invent one was correct)

evals.prompt: Set up two reviewers on this design, one of them codex.
evals.expected_output: Fires. The mix is stated explicitly: exactly one of the two seats is Codex, and the composition is announced before the seats run.
expectations: Runs exactly two seats, exactly one of them Codex
Gives the Codex seat the job of disagreeing, not the summarising job
States the composition BEFORE running, naming which seat is Codex
Attributes each finding to its seat in the result
evals.covers: composition: an explicit ratio is honoured exactly and announced

evals.prompt: Tear this migration plan apart from every angle you can think of. No codex, just you.
evals.expected_output: Fires only to read the composition rule, then runs ZERO Codex seats. 'No codex' overrides the panel default.
expectations: Runs no Codex seats at all
Does NOT argue for a Codex seat or add one 'for decorrelation'
Still says plainly that the panel is all-Claude and therefore shares one bias
evals.covers: composition: an explicit zero overrides the default, and the cost is stated not hidden

evals.prompt: Fix the failing test in packages/core. Only codex.
evals.expected_output: Fires. 'Only codex' applies to single-agent work too: Codex does the task, the coordinator orchestrates and verifies rather than doing it.
expectations: Hands the task itself to Codex rather than doing it directly
Uses --level write in a worktree, not --level read, because the task edits files
Still verifies the result independently (--verify or reading the command list)
Says up front that Codex is doing the work
evals.covers: composition: the scale applies to a single agent, not only to panels

evals.prompt: Get a second opinion on whether this lock implementation is actually correct.
evals.expected_output: Fires. Nothing was said about the mix, so the default applies: a disagreeing seat goes to Codex, and that is stated up front.
expectations: Includes at least one Codex seat under the default
Announces that the second opinion is coming from Codex before running it
Does NOT silently substitute a Claude seat if the Codex seat returns nothing
evals.covers: composition: the unstated default puts the dissenting seat on Codex

evals.prompt: Сделай ревью этого диффа, и половину работы отдай codex.
evals.expected_output: Fires. The user names Codex and states the mix (half); Russian phrasing must trigger like English.
expectations: Invokes the codex-delegate skill
Honours the stated half-codex mix
Announces the composition before the seats run
evals.covers: trigger (ru): user names Codex and a mix

evals.prompt: Собери панель из четырёх ревьюеров, пусть разнесут этот дизайн перед тем, как я закоммичусь.
evals.expected_output: Fires. A review panel needs a decorrelated seat; no English keyword present — semantic match must carry it.
expectations: Considers giving at least one seat to Codex via codex-delegate
Does NOT hand the whole panel to Codex
evals.covers: trigger (ru): panel with no codex/gpt token

evals.prompt: Проверь моё решение через gpt — пусть попробует его опровергнуть.
evals.expected_output: Fires. 'через gpt' is in the description's trigger list verbatim.
expectations: Invokes the codex-delegate skill
Chooses --level read
evals.covers: trigger (ru): user names GPT

evals.prompt: Переименуй файл codex-delegate.test.ts в delegate.test.ts и поправь импорты.
evals.expected_output: Stays silent. 'codex' as part of a filename is not a delegation request — the Russian mirror of case 9.
expectations: Does NOT invoke the codex-delegate skill
Just renames the file
evals.covers: negative (ru): skill name inside a filename
